hints.title: Step Cost Minimization Obstacle
hints.text: Reaching each stair requires stepping from either one or two steps below. How can calculating the cheapest cumulative expenditure to reach previous steps determine the optimal cost for all subsequent stairs?

hints.title: Optimal Substructure Recurrence Invariant
hints.text: The cheapest cost to reach step i is the cost of step i plus the minimum of the cheapest cumulative costs to reach step i - 1 and step i - 2.

hints.title: Constant Space Rolling Accumulation Procedure
hints.text: Maintain two scalar variables representing the minimum cumulative cost to reach the previous two steps. Iterate from the third step up to the top, updating the rolling minimums by adding the current stair cost to the smaller predecessor. Return the minimum of the final two values.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: A single linear scan updates two scalar accumulators.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Branching recursively on every 1 or 2 step choice takes O(2^N) exponential time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Storing full table takes O(N) space, while two scalar registers achieve O(1) space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Reducing auxiliary space from O(N) to O(1) by maintaining only the last two states.
